Support routines for demand-paged workspaces and solfuzz runner setup, teardown, and leak checks.

# Purpose
`fd_solfuzz.c` provides support routines for a Solana fuzzing runner that uses a shared-memory workspace. The file defines [`fd_wksp_demand_paged_new`](<#fd_wksp_demand_paged_new>) and [`fd_wksp_demand_paged_delete`](<#fd_wksp_demand_paged_delete>) to create and destroy a workspace from anonymous demand-paged memory, with huge-page alignment and `madvise( ..., MADV_HUGEPAGE )` to request huge-page backing. It also registers the memory as an anonymous shared-memory region so the workspace can be managed through the shared-memory layer used by the rest of the code base.

The file also defines the lifecycle for `fd_solfuzz_runner_t` objects. [`fd_solfuzz_runner_new`](<#fd_solfuzz_runner_new>) allocates and initializes the runner and its internal objects, including `fd_funk` instances, account database joins, program cache joins, a scratch pad, and bank state. [`fd_solfuzz_runner_delete`](<#fd_solfuzz_runner_delete>) releases those objects and frees the workspace allocations. [`fd_solfuzz_runner_leak_check`](<#fd_solfuzz_runner_leak_check>) verifies that the runner does not leave a `spad` frame or a `funk` transaction open, and it reports a critical error if it finds leaked state.
